summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded systems software development experience in C and C++ across STM32 microcontrollers, Arduino, Raspberry Pi and NVIDIA Jetson. Built bare-metal firmware driving GPIO, timer, ADC and I2C peripherals directly, and multi-microcontroller systems coordinated over UART with FreeRTOS task synchronization. Debugs on hardware with oscilloscopes and logic analyzers, root-causing integration failures to a fix.

Embedded Software: Microcontroller peripherals (GPIO, TIM, ADC, I2C, UART)

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with a Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; root-caused sensor jitter and resolved it through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication and integration end-to-end.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 microcontroller peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) at 3.68 KB Flash and 1.58 KB RAM, holding a deterministic 1 Hz update rate.
Built Cortex-M4 monitoring firmware with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Coordinated shared-memory tasks under FreeRTOS with mutexes, alongside interrupt-driven UART command handling with user override.
Ran YOLOv8 on an NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an STM32 microcontroller over UART across a two-processor system.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) - MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Root-caused and resolved 11 integration failures on hardware (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture), reaching 100% pick reliability over 10/10 trials at ~11.5 s end-to-end latency.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics in C++ on Arduino, driving five servos with contact detection from dual VL53L0X ToF sensors gating the grasp at 25 mm.
